note.note:
Consult Summary:
27-year-old patient with known asthma reports 2–3 days of increased shortness of breath, wheeze and cough unresponsive to usual salbutamol. Advised to increase inhaled steroid dose, optimise reliever use, and attend face-to-face GP review or A&E if deterioration.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation (mild–moderate)
- Onset/progression: Began 2–3 days ago during a run; now symptomatic with brisk walking.  
- Symptoms: Shortness of breath, wheeze, non-productive cough; no sputum, no hospital admission required.  
- Current control: Previously stable; last asthma attack 3–4 years ago; last asthma review ~2 years ago.  
- Medications: Salbutamol (blue) inhaler PRN; Clenil (brown/beclometasone) inhaler 3 puffs BID (patient recalled); uses blue inhaler daily at present without relief.  
- Pertinent negatives: No fever, no chest pain, no productive sputum.  
- Objective data: Usual peak flow ≈380 L/min (no current reading).  
- Plan discussed: Increase Clenil to 4 puffs BID; salbutamol up to every 2 hours PRN; arrange urgent in-person GP review for chest exam and peak-flow; consider oral steroids/antibiotics depending on findings; attend A&E if breathing worsens despite measures.

Issue 2: Possible eczema
- History of dry/itchy skin; currently using Cetraben emollient and topical hydrocortisone.  
- No acute concerns raised.

Issue 3: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
- Patient states “I have hay fever.” No active management discussed.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (reliever, currently PRN up to Q2H).
- Clenil (beclometasone) inhaler – previously 3 puffs BID; advised to increase to 4 puffs BID.
- Cetraben cream – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hydrocortisone topical – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- “Flanel/Bactroban” (exact medication unclear; conflict noted).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (diagnosed childhood, never hospitalised, no prior oral steroids).
- Possible eczema (patient-reported).
- Hay fever.

Social History:
- Not discussed (smoking, alcohol, occupation, living arrangements undocumented).

Preventative History:
- Last asthma nurse review ≈2 years ago.
- Other routine screenings/vaccinations not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or examination performed during video consult.

Plan:
- Book urgent face-to-face GP appointment for chest examination and peak-flow measurement in next few days.
- Increase Clenil to 4 puffs twice daily until review.
- Use salbutamol inhaler up to every 2 hours as needed for symptoms.
- Seek emergency care (A&E) if breathlessness worsens despite above or if using salbutamol very frequently.
- GP to consider oral prednisolone course and/or antibiotics after assessment.
- Arrange follow-up asthma review and update action plan post-exacerbation.
- Ensure inhaler technique checked at next visit; consider providing home peak-flow meter.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing expected elements: vitals, smoking/alcohol history, full medication list with doses, drug allergy status confirmed but environmental allergies only; peak-flow not measured today.  
● Internal conflicts: Unclear inhaler regimen (patient states using blue inhaler “morning or evening to prevent” symptoms; preventive inhaler colour/name briefly confusing); mention of “Flanel Bactroban” unclear.  
● Transcript quality: Moderate; occasional audio gaps and unclear medication names, but main clinical details interpretable.
